html:
SMTO-GWT-0062 — Your graphics card doesn't support this action

GUID: a335063a-d114-5d67-9bf0-1c8bbcc523ac
Slug: gpu-metric-unsupported
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • The graphics card (GPU) or its driver on that computer doesn't offer this feature, so SMTO didn't do it. No GPU settings were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to show the details for this GPU and which settings it can change (for example, "show details for GPU 0"). The details show which settings this card and driver report, such as power limit, persistence mode or compute mode.
  2. Pick a different action that the details show as supported, or leave this setting as it is. SMTO won't try a feature the card says it doesn't have, so asking for the same one again gives the same result.
  3. If you expected this feature to work, ask the person who manages the GPU computer to confirm it runs Linux with a current NVIDIA driver. Some features, such as persistence mode, are only offered on Linux and only when the installed NVIDIA tools include them.

What success looks like

  • A supported action finishes and SMTO reports its result, or you decide to leave the setting unchanged.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the computer with the GPU. Don't keep asking SMTO to repeat the same request; the card will refuse it the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The NVIDIA provider classified the requested GPU metric or operation as unsupported (nvidia-smi exit code 3 or 13), or persistence-mode control is unavailable in the device's current capability profile.

What this means

  • The provider classified the requested metric or operation as unsupported, or persistence-mode capability was absent in the current device profile. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The provider classified the requested metric or operation as unsupported, or persistence-mode capability was absent in the current device profile.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the specific operation and current capability report; unavailable telemetry is distinct from a value of zero.

How to fix it

  • Check the device's reported values and capability flags with gpu.device, gpu.power_limits or gpu.clock_capabilities for the UUID; persistence control requires a Linux Gateway, a non-null persistence_mode and --persistence-mode in the installed nvidia-smi help. Use an operation the device reports as supported, or update the NVIDIA driver on the Gateway host if the feature should exist.
  • Inspect the device capabilities and use supported operations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the device capabilities and use supported operations.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported operation returns a valid result, or the unsupported requirement is explicitly left unmet.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
